0. Executive decisions / immutable design principles

NERDS = Navigation & Expedition Research Discovery Suite; offline-first, independent conventional algorithms for discovery, routing, project management, numerical validation and Captain-facing presentation.
4nR-SURVEYOR = independent local AI research & orchestration application with six logical agents; returns source-aware research, evidence and recommendations, never silent navigational control.
4nR-MOS = collective shipboard software ecosystem and documentation authority, not a third executable repository; MCP is the Master Control Program concept.
USER PATH = unrestricted editable path anywhere on Earth, like Google Earth Pro Add Path. Drawing never depends on hydrographic, road, vessel or weather evidence.
Four separate progressive route analyses; BY-WAY first, then stage choices. BY-SEA selected by default; BY-LAND/BY-AIR disable Stages 3–4.
BY-SEA operational modes default BYPASS: use USER-defined speed ONLY, initially 6 knots; engineering parameters nullable, NULL is not zero.
All core engines and available geographic datasets should be integrated and managed by NERDS; installation SIZE IS NOT A CONSTRAINT, but performance and reliability are.
All previously approved source details preserved in the archival appendices. Conflict decisions are recorded explicitly below.
Engineering directive: MAKE IT WORK. MAKE IT FAST. MAKE IT AWESOME. IT CAN BE HUGE.
1. MOS/MCP — high-level software architecture

The MOS software scope unifies expedition planning, research intelligence and future departmental software interfaces. Shipboard equipment has its own controllers, protection systems, mechanical/electrical design documents and safety procedures. MOS may observe, model, log and where specifically authorised exchange commands, but general-purpose software and AI are not substitutes for independent safety controllers.
Domain
Responsibility / boundary
NERDS
Globes and UI, unrestricted path drawing, routing stages, ship profiles, geographic/road/water/weather datasets, local calculations, project persistence, decision records.
4nR-SURVEYOR

MCP integration role

Departmental equipment
Continues to operate under its own hardware/PLC/BMS/ECU/fire/security systems, following separate engineering documentation.
Captain & USER
Approve itinerary changes, operational choices and vessel actions; AI recommendation alone cannot trigger control actions.
1.1 Common cross-system obligations
No compulsory AI inference or continuous Internet for NERDS core operations.
Dataset source/licence/version/checksum and updated timestamps remain traceable.
Local-first data acquisition, offline caching, background checks, atomic updates, validation, rollback and recovery.
Human authority, role-based permissions, auditability, explicit confirmed actions for consequential changes.
Integration interfaces versioned; consumers tolerate absent SURVEYOR or absent future departmental modules.
Separate development repositories, processes, logs, deployments and acceptance tests.
2. NERDS — AUTHORITATIVE CURRENT REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Object model: USER PATH, course stages & route segments

USER PATH is the USER-authored ordered sequence of geographically referenced vertices. This is not itself a claim of a viable road, marine or air passage. Calculated routes are versioned derived results associated with a particular USER PATH revision, BY-WAY, vessel snapshot, data versions and stage settings. The USER can view any preserved stage result without overwriting the underlying USER PATH.

2.2 USER PATH — exact globe interactions
Interaction
Required action & edge case
Single left-click in EDIT USER PATH
Create/insert vertex at clicked WGS84 globe point. No requirement for geographic connectivity or navigability. Click existing markers/labels/controls must not create spurious vertices.
Double left-click on vertex
Delete selected USER PATH vertex, cancel pending single-click insertion and preserve undo state. Must not delete unrelated destination record.
Left-click hold & drag vertex
Reposition vertex geographically; on release update affected path geometry, numerical coarse distances and invalidate stale derived results.
Right-click vertex
Context menu: marker pin/star/other shapes, 00–99 number or none, text label or none, colour/size/visibility, properties, coordinate copy and reset options.
Left-click hold & drag LABEL
Move label only, not geographic vertex. Retain screen-space label offset as globe moves; leader line appears when displaced as needed.
Double-click LABEL
Edit label text without deleting path vertex. Event precedence must be tested.
Right-click LABEL
Appearance, visibility and reset label placement, without invoking globe pan/zoom.
Empty globe (not in path insertion mode)
Normal Cesium navigation; dedicated modes avoid conflict with selection, pin placement, camera drag or double-click zoom.
UNDO / REDO
Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y for add/delete/move/rename/relabel/icon/number edits; action history coherently invalidates derived route caches.

Marker numbers 00–99 are optional display metadata and not unique primary keys; more than 100 vertices are permitted. Auto and manual numbering, duplicates and conflict warnings require explicit deterministic UI rules. Label movement never changes route coordinates, calculations or evidence.

2.5 Geographic BY-SEA and refinement engineering

Acquire systematic WORLDWIDE marine, rivers, lakes, reservoirs, canals, deltas, estuaries and water-area/coastal data by planned datasets, basins and tiles. Named test routes remain REGRESSION CASES, not the global acquisition programme.

Preserve exact network/source connectivity, bounds, islands/holes, ownership, dataset integrity and verified ocean-network transitions. Distinguish source-backed route, provisional connector and unsupported routing; do not fabricate verified waterways.
COARSE simplifies grid-cell staircase into direct geography-validated segments where corridor is supported. High-resolution detail must derive from finer real sources, not just extra points.

User can add, remove and drag manually constrained CALCULATED COURSE vertices in separate EDIT COURSE mode; valid source/network recalculation, persistent constraints, undo/redo and event disambiguation are required.

Visual Cesium spline/LOD is presentation-only. Global zoom smooth, closer zoom exposes actual course vertices. Neither smoothing nor labels changes canonical geometry, WGS84 geodesic nautical miles or ETAs. No deceptive smoothing over land.
Retain original coarse route as immutable comparison snapshot for a given input revision and a separate detailed/refined variant. Preserve success of unaffected legs when a leg is unresolved.

Geographic connectivity and navigability are distinct; Beta first draws unrestricted PATH, next generates proposed connected itineraries and separately assesses geographic evidence. Suitability constraints remain optional advisories unless explicitly selected.
2.6 BY-LAND — integrated offline road network

NERDS SHALL implement real road-following BY-LAND routing with current, locally cached, updateable road databases. Evaluate Valhalla as preferred integrated candidate, including Windows x64 packaging and lifecycle testing; not yet an adopted tested implementation. OSM licence compliance and data provenance mandatory. The user must not separately install Docker, Python or launch a routing service. Actual roads, junctions, restrictions, road classifications and relevant speed profiles determine distances & estimated duration. Missing coverage must be identified as approximate/unresolved, never represented as real connected roads.
Background automatic ROAD DATA checks default ON; atomic tile update, integrity checks, rollback and offline retained prior verified version.
LIVE TRAFFIC default OFF and no traffic requests unless USER enables; temporary incidents have expiration timestamps and separate provider/licence validation.
Online data updating works when connectivity available; shipboard/offline local cache always remains usable.
Road updates and live traffic are separate datasets and separate USER preferences.
2.7 BY-AIR — independent mode

BY-AIR Stage 1 geodesic baseline; Stage 2 uses supported air-route/airport information and appropriate aircraft or scheduled airline assumptions when available. No invented airline schedules, fares or airspace clearances. Record aircraft speed/range, data provenance, airport identifiers, uncertainties and provisional segments distinctly. Stages 3–4 disabled.
2.8 Global data-management service
Subdomain
Operational requirement
Data acquisition
Built-in downloads, updates and integrity checks; local gazetteer, marine, water, road and forecast sources; no external installation burden.
Coverage
Worldwide data coverage view: installed / available / downloading / stale / unsupported; regions selectable without prior provider knowledge.
Update defaults
Road-data periodic ON; live traffic OFF; marine/geographic periodic updates user-configurable; forecasts expire according to valid time.
Reliability
Resume/retry bounded requests, hashes, licence records, timestamp, version, atomic replacement, rollback, acquisition budget and logs.
Data footprint
Installer and datasets may be large; use appropriate tile caches and lazy loading for runtime performance; user may choose regions without global product limitations.
2.9 UI, project recovery & workflows
Preserve accepted WORLD/FIT/FOCUS; adjustable 1-second hover geographic identification (0.5–5 s), context menu at exact coordinate, coordinate formats, Segoe UI and map annotation preferences.
USER PATH and route result visibility independent; separate colours/patterns for sea #153B78 solid, land #FF2525 solid, RIB #39BDF2 dashed, air #00D65A dashed, provisional amber #E5A126 rounded dots.
Simple stage-switch action uses cached compatible output; input change invalidates affected downstream results, not other unrelated saved variants.
Autosave/recovery after crash with atomic writes; SAVE, SAVE AS, OPEN; clear restore/discard semantics; user-preference versus per-project state separated.
Desktop state preserves draggable labels, marker icons, all vertices, stage outputs, provenance, ship snapshots and status across restart.
Future dockable multi-monitor workspace as originally approved; keep panel state modular now.
Background computation shows progress and CANCEL; cancel preserves prior accepted results and original USER PATH.
2.10 Non-AI/N-application interface

NERDS core must be independent of inference, Lemonade and SURVEYOR. NERDS may issue explicitly authorised, versioned research requests and receive evidence/proposals; geographic/numeric results verified by local deterministic algorithms; Captain approves any itinerary changes. SURVEYOR absence cannot block PATH editing, routing, offline discovery or saved project access.
3. 4nR-SURVEYOR — latest consolidated scope

SURVEYOR is the independent advanced AI gatekeeper and orchestrator of six logical specialist research agents. It runs separately from NERDS, uses local inference/analytical tools, maintains its own evidence archive, model inventory and test infrastructure, and exchanges source-aware structured results. Full v2.5 source requirements are attached verbatim in Appendix C.

3.1 Runtime, autonomy & verification

AMD Ryzen AI Max/Strix Halo 128GB local evaluation platform; Lemonade Server v2026.41.1 and Qwen3-30B-A3B GGUF llama.cpp ROCm were initial experimentally operational local baseline. Do not claim six agents operational.
No six independent massive model installations required; specialist configurations, analytic tools and candidate models selected after performance/licence/quality evaluation.
Agent research returns citations, provenance, evidence quality, limitations, assumptions and recommendations; no autonomous change of Captain-approved voyage plan.
Self-evaluation proposals require reproducible tests and recorded rejection/deferral history before adoption.
No shared writable database or required live AI dependency for NERDS; project architecture permits distinct onboard machines.
Specialist forecast/intelligence can enrich NERDS WEATHER ROUTE, but deterministic numerical route calculation and ownership remain NERDS responsibilities.

The newer v2.5 scope is available as a complete local working DOCX and is attached here. No independently verified operational parent runtime or agent implementations in the remote repository. The README references docs/MODEL_EVALUATION.md, docs/NERDS_INTEGRATION.md, docs/STATUS.md and agents/README.md, which were NOT found on the remote default branch during verification. Do not claim their presence.

Application Scope & Development Baseline — v0.2.1
14 October 2026  |  Status: planning scope for review  |  Repository: clarkgraff/NERDS

Scope boundary: NERDS is the expedition navigation, geographic & vessel-planning application. 4nR-SURVEYOR is a separate, independently versioned research intelligence system. Their integration is optional and governed by an explicit interface. This document does not replace the standalone 4nR-SURVEYOR scope.
1. Purpose & release definition

NERDS supports planning and evaluating a global maritime expedition through an offline-first geographic workspace. It must manage waypoints, visualise routes, estimate passage distance & time, apply vessel characteristics, and prepare the foundation for progressively more sophisticated marine and environmental routing.

v0.2.1 is the target specification for the next navigational development milestone, not a declaration that these features have been built or validated. Codex has unfinished work in progress; the actual repository state must be inspected and reconciled before implementation.
2. Separation of systems — mandatory architecture
NERDS: owns  |  4nR-SURVEYOR: owns
Waypoints, route plans, marine geometry, chart layers  |  Cultural investigation, discovery & research preferences
Vessel specifications, passage estimates, route alternatives  |  Nine SURVEYOR disciplinary classification frameworks
Weather/current/tide visualisation and computational routing  |  AI reasoning, research indexing, source provenance & knowledge synthesis
Expedition geographic project storage & export  |  Independent research archive, profile persistence & research reports
Either system must start and operate its core functions when the other is unavailable.
No shared writable database, hidden runtime coupling, or requirement to have a local language model installed to plan routes.
Define a versioned, documented exchange interface for waypoint IDs, coordinates, route IDs, time windows and referenced findings; support explicit import/export or local API later.
The legacy “4nR-AI” connection dialog in v0.1.0 is an integration prototype; its continued placement inside NERDS is not an architectural requirement.

4. Geographic workspace & mapping
Retain CesiumJS globe with 2D Mercator switching, zoom, pan, selection, geolocated waypoints and clear route overlays.
Operate offline from packaged or bunkered base imagery at an appropriate, documented level of detail; online layers may be added without breaking offline use.
Support selected location, labelled waypoint sequence, leg information, overview fit and visible distinction between proposed geometry and validated marine routes.
Track layer provenance, licence, geographic coverage, resolution, time relevance and offline availability.
Base map, coastlines, bathymetry, administrative geography and marine chart data are separate datasets with distinct reliability and licensing.
5. WAYPOINTS & expedition project model
Create, edit, rename, delete and reorder waypoints; drag-and-drop and explicit move-up/down controls must keep the map in sync.
Permit city lookup, manual lat/long entry and map-pin placement; do not force city-centre coordinates to represent a vessel berth or harbour entrance.
Maintain stable waypoint identifiers independent of list order; distinguish place of interest, port access location, transit waypoint and optional land-visit waypoint.
Store leg endpoints, transport mode (BY-SEA default; BY-ROAD / BY-AIR when deliberately selected), schedule data, notes, source and coordinate precision.
Persist multiple named expedition projects, reopen accurately, recover safely from interrupted writes and export in documented formats.
Compute leg nautical miles, cumulative nautical miles, travel-time estimate & arrival projection from the route geometry actually in use; mark provisional values.
6. VESSEL PREFERENCES
Attribute group  |  Required inputs / calculations
Identification  |  Vessel name, flag/country, IMO, MMSI, image/icon.
Geometry  |  Length overall, beam, draft, air draft, displacement; hull type; optional waterline length.
Propulsion  |  Independent SAIL, POWER-DIESEL & POWER-ELECTRIC selections; supported combinations.
Operating performance  |  Editable nominal speeds, estimated hull speed from waterline length when applicable, manual override, modes BEST-TIME / BEST-EFFICIENCY / BEST-SAILING.
Route constraints  |  Configurable under-keel clearance, bridge clearance & draft/air-draft safety allowances; provenance of assumptions.

The ship model should be designed for later extension with sail polars, motor efficiency curves, hybrid energy characteristics, sea-state response and learned performance from measured telemetry. Those advanced models are not presumed already calibrated in v0.2.1.
6A. Offshore routing & dual voyage estimates — approved requirements

Default speeds — The expedition-wide reference speed is 6.0 knots, editable in VESSEL PREFERENCES. The nominal target cruising speed under POWER-DIESEL or POWER-ELECTRIC is 10.0 knots, also editable. These are planning assumptions, not guaranteed actual speeds.

Side-by-side passage display — For every leg and the whole voyage, display STANDARD (6.0 kn) and CALCULATED estimates adjacent to one another. Show reference speed, modelled effective speed over ground (SOG), passage distance (NM), elapsed duration, projected arrival date/time and the time difference. Never replace the 6-knot baseline with the calculated figure.

Power-mode accounting — When powered propulsion is selected, use the 10.0-knot nominal target as an input to the calculated passage case; retain the 6.0-knot baseline for direct comparison. Sailing nominal target begins at 6.0 kn. For mixed sail/power routing, compute elapsed time by segment according to its operating mode and integrate segment times rather than averaging segment speeds.

Dynamic recalculation — Recalculate the CALCULATED estimate after changes to route geometry, distance, propulsion mode, vessel preferences or available wind/current/wave data. Until numerical environmental integration is available, calculate a clearly labelled nominal-speed estimate; do not display synthetic weather-derived values as measured or forecast speeds.

Effective voyage speed — Calculate end-to-end effective SOG as total route distance divided by summed travel time. Estimate ETA from departure date/time plus elapsed time; distinguish vessel-local clock displays from underlying stored timestamps.

Offshore preferred routing — Include OFFSHORE PREFERRED as a routing preference. Penalise unnecessary coastline proximity, mapped reefs/shoals and unsuitable or uncertain depths; consider continental shelf, shelf break, slope and abrupt seabed rises as contextual factors. Shelf-break alignment is NOT a mandatory routing track.

Coastal separation — Provide an editable preferred minimum separation from land in nautical miles (suggested choices: 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 and Custom). This is a soft optimisation preference, not an absolute constraint, particularly for harbour approaches, canals, straits and rivers.

Clearance and geological context — Under-keel clearance, coastal hazards and chart restrictions remain separate evidence-dependent checks. Detect charted underwater obstructions where data supports them. Geological/seismic/volcanic hazards, if added later, require their own datasets; seabed gradients alone do not predict activity.

Staged implementation — For v0.2.1, implement editable nominal speeds and paired baseline/nominal-calculated duration & ETA outputs against actual route geometry; add route-preference storage and explicit status for preliminary offshore routing. Bathymetry-aware clearance, authoritative coastal constraints and real forecast optimisation remain staged by available datasets and validation.
7. Global marine routing — staged implementation
7.1 Foundational water-aware routing
Generate route candidates between water-access endpoints over an explicit marine graph or accessible-water surface, avoiding mapped land at the dataset’s working resolution.
Apply route connections from city/interest coordinates to maritime access points separately; label them as connectors, not sea passages.
Implement transparent fallback when the dataset cannot resolve a narrow channel, lock, canal or approach; never silently claim a valid passage.
Preserve alternatives and annotate routing provenance, coverage and confidence. A visually plausible ocean route is not proof of navigational clearance.
7.2 Marine restrictions & chart awareness
Treat coastline screening, bathymetric clearance, official nautical chart features, restricted areas and bridge clearances as different validation layers.
Depth/under-keel, air draft, canals, locks, traffic restrictions and known passage exclusions must be modelled as typed constraints, with unavailable evidence explicitly reported.
Use high-resolution authoritative regional data when available. Global GEBCO-scale depth grids are useful for context but do not establish safe harbour/channel transits.
7.3 Scope of data acquisition
NO BULK DOWNLOAD of the complete NOAA United States ENC/chart database. Acquire only chosen regional data relevant to a route when appropriate and licensed.
Stage global low-resolution coastline and bathymetry as separate layers; define update cadence, licences, space requirements and geographic coverage.
Use Store & Forward bunkering for selective coastal, environmental and route-area content, storing verification metadata and source attribution.
8. Environmental routing & visualisation
Provide a data-layer interface for winds, currents, waves, weather systems and tides, distinguishing observation, analysis and forecast with timestamp and valid-time metadata.
Integrate appropriately licensed environmental visualisation techniques inspired by the MIT-licensed Cameron Beccario Earth project while preserving full licence/copyright notices for reused code.
Keep environmental rendering distinct from routing computation; use physically meaningful forecast grids, units and interpolation, not the visual particle animation as a numerical routing engine.
Specify separate routing objective functions for BEST-TIME, BEST-EFFICIENCY and BEST-SAILING. Estimate ETAs and vessel responses only to the precision supported by available data.
Provide fallback routes when environmental datasets are unavailable; display data-age and uncertainty indicators.
9. Calculations, testing & verification
Acceptance area  |  Minimum objective
Geometry  |  No sea-route leg crosses mapped land at the tested dataset resolution; source & resolution documented.
Waypoint editing  |  Reordering updates list, numbering, polyline, distances & persisted project consistently.
Passage accounting  |  Leg, total NM, elapsed time and ETA recalculate deterministically from current routing geometry & operating speed.
Vessel constraints  |  Draft/air-draft restrictions are applied if authoritative evidence exists; otherwise show unresolved status, not clearance.
Offline mode  |  Open projects, edit waypoints, view cached globe and use available routing layers with network disconnected.
Data integrity  |  Restart/reopen preserves coordinates, project, vessel settings, mode, selected route and citations.
Regression  |  Automated geometry/unit/project tests plus desktop smoke tests and a reproducible MSI install.

Dual voyage estimates  |  Every leg and total voyage show a constant 6.0 kn reference beside a separate calculated/nominal estimate, both with duration & ETA; changing route geometry recalculates both.
Powered voyage  |  Selecting POWER uses editable nominal 10.0 kn for the calculated case while retaining the 6.0 kn reference; mixed propulsion sums segment durations.
Offshore planning preference  |  A saved preference includes OFFSHORE PREFERRED and editable coastline separation; any unvalidated chart/bathymetric safety conclusions are clearly identified.

Suggested validation passages: Amsterdam → Emden → Hamburg → Kiel → Gdańsk (including coastal and confined-water cases); an open-ocean passage such as Lisbon → Casablanca; and a route where a direct great-circle line crosses land. Test cases must declare available chart depth, coastline scale and expected unresolved constraints.
10. User interface & output
Keep navigation tasks accessible from ROUTE PLOT and geographic display, with a visible vessel-profile editor and leg-level results.
Separate “PLANNING DEMONSTRATION”, “PRELIMINARY WATER-AWARE ROUTE” and “CHART-CONSTRAINED ROUTE” statuses according to demonstrated capabilities.
On the map and in exports, show route geometry, waypoints, NM, timestamps, objective mode, dataset provenance, warnings and unresolved validation gaps.
Preserve field notes and production references as optional waypoint metadata; detailed cultural research remains the separate 4nR-SURVEYOR responsibility.
11. Release engineering & handoff
Inspect the live repository first, including its current branch, open modifications, tests and Codex reports; do not overwrite unfinished work or recreate already implemented features.
Produce an incremental commit trail, change log, test report, known limitations, packaging/build instructions and versioned Windows MSI.
Use a clear release label v0.2.1 only after implemented acceptance tests pass; describe incomplete features as deferred rather than delivered.
Design NERDS APIs and project schema for forward compatibility with a separate 4nR-SURVEYOR process; no cross-project integration work until separately approved.

REVISION C — Worldwide Waypoint Discovery & Clean Workspace
14 October 2026  |  Status: approved v0.2.1 amendment | REVISION C supersedes conflicting wording in Revision B and all earlier scope sections.
C1. Remove starter-city demonstrations

Completely remove the existing list of fifteen starter cities, its hardcoded selection UI, and any seed data or startup logic that inserts demonstration waypoints. Do not repurpose that list as a production lookup catalogue.

Every new project starts with ZERO waypoints and an uncluttered globe. Any future user demonstration must be separately invoked, such as a dedicated video or example-project command, and must never prepopulate a newly created live project.
All selectable lists and disambiguation results should be alphabetical when alphabetical ordering is appropriate; route waypoint order remains user-defined, never auto-alphabetised.
C2. Three waypoint creation workflows
CITY LOOKUP: search globally for cities, towns, villages and named geographic places; allow selection and creation of an editable waypoint.
PLACE MAP PIN: click any coordinate on the globe to create a named waypoint, including an anchorage or uninhabited position.
MANUAL COORDINATES: create or revise a waypoint by entering a name and geographic latitude/longitude.
All three paths must support editing, deletion, drag-reordering, map synchronisation, persistence and project reopen. The map and list must keep stable waypoint IDs independent of order.
C3. Offline worldwide gazetteer & connected fallback

Use GeoNames as the proposed initial worldwide gazetteer, subject to suitability and compliance with its attribution and licence. Package or locally install a globally useful place-name index; do not depend on active internet access to find ordinary cities.

Implement responsive local indexed search; offer optional online lookup for missing or ambiguous entries when connected. Evaluate OpenStreetMap-derived geocoding for richer place details, observing third-party service rate/use restrictions and licensing.

Show location name, country, administrative region and relevant coordinates in disambiguation choices. Preserve local-language names and alternate spellings where the source data provides them. No arbitrary restriction to fifteen or any other short fixed list.
Record each resolved place source, source ID, resolution method and any user coordinate override. Document data provenance, attribution, update procedure, offline coverage and source licences.
C4. Geographic anchors & routing

For recognised cities, prefer City Hall/municipal-centre coordinates when reliably obtainable. Fall back to the documented geographic city centre; for map-pin and manual waypoints, retain exactly the user-selected coordinates.

PLOT ROUTE must not require a user to manually assign a water-access point. Coarse marine routing should identify approximate land-to-water connectors and offshore traversals from location anchors, clearly distinguishing non-navigable connectors from actual water route segments.

The city-hall-to-city-hall workflow is a preliminary global planning capability; refined harbour, inland-waterway, chart-constrained and clearance-aware navigation is staged for later development. Display this uncertainty in UI and exports.
C5. Acceptance tests & implementation boundaries
AF-003 passes only if an entirely new project starts with exactly zero waypoints, no starter-city selector and no demo route.

AF-004 passes only if offline search resolves representative cities across multiple continents with disambiguation; connected fallback provides additional locations; users can add locations from results without manual water-access setup.
Test adding a location through each of CITY LOOKUP, PLACE MAP PIN and MANUAL COORDINATES; reorder, edit, save, close and reopen to confirm persistence.

Preserve existing passed waypoint drag-and-drop and SAVE PROJECT behaviour. Keep v0.2.1 Rev B global dialogue, time zone, vessel, routing, overlays and build-quality requirements unchanged except where explicitly superseded here.
NERDS and 4nR-SURVEYOR remain separate applications, sharing only a documented optional exchange interface; SURVEYOR map hints are externally supplied layers.

1. PRIORITY 1 — ROUTING ENGINE REPAIRS
1.1 Correct mixed-grid routing defects

The current source uses worldwide 0.1° and European 0.025° land/water masks. The access-point resolver can select endpoints in different grids before a leg is computed using one routing grid. A candidate water cell in one grid can therefore be blocked in the grid used to calculate the leg.
Select a compatible routing network for each leg before choosing BOTH access points.
Resolve both endpoints against the selected network; verify the water status and connectivity of each cell.
Handle regional grid transitions consistently; do not rely on ad hoc per-port exceptions.
Log waypoint IDs, coordinate pairs, grid selection, access candidates, cell classification, search bounds and errors.
Regression pairs: Barcelona → Ibiza; Algiers → Marseille; Lisbon → A Coruña.
1.2 Connected ocean, coastal & inland-waterway routing

Replace reliance on the coarse ocean mask alone with network-aware connections for rivers, estuaries, canals, lakes, straits and harbours. Test the source geometry and topology before adjusting the pathfinder. A river centreline does not alone establish navigability or suitability for The Faire Wind.
Priority waterways: Amazon and tributaries; St. Lawrence / Great Lakes; Thames; Elbe; Tagus; Gironde/Garonne; North Sea Canal; Mediterranean straits and principal harbour entrances.
Acquire suitable data through a documented geographic-data layer; consider OSM-derived navigable-waterway geometry and relevant hydrological/hydrographic authorities.
Distinguish actual waterways, verified navigable segments and unresolved connectivity. Maintain vessel draft and air-clearance constraints for future refinement.
Do not generate a fictitious distant offshore detour for two points on a connected inland waterway.
1.3 Independent voyage-leg processing & fault isolation
Calculate each adjacent waypoint pair independently, preserving previous successful legs if another leg fails.
Continue computing later legs when feasible, returning per-leg success, failure and evidence.
Do not erase a successful itinerary merely because a newly added waypoint has unresolved access.
Present provisional amber rounded-dot connection for unresolved geography with a specific reason.
1.4 Routing preferences — baseline BYPASS

During engine diagnosis set OFFSHORE PREFERRED, coastal separation and optional routing penalties to BYPASS. Preserve existing feature code and settings for later revalidation; do not delete them. Use geography and connected navigability as the mandatory route constraints. The desired default preference for new projects is AUTO after baseline verification, with other preferences available for subsequent refinement.
1.5 Accurate distance & time accounting
Separate CALCULATED DISTANCE, PROVISIONAL DISTANCE, TOTAL ESTIMATED DISTANCE and their time equivalents.
Never report unresolved 0.0 NM / 0h 0m as though a journey has been completed.
If a provisional distance cannot be estimated credibly, show UNRESOLVED, not a fabricated figure.
Keep reference speed (6 kn) and calculated operating-speed information, ETA and explicit UTC/time-zone representation intact.
2. PRIORITY 2 — ROUTE PLOT OPERATING LOGIC
2.1 PLOT FIRST. REFINE SECOND.

Only two valid waypoints are required to enable PLOT ROUTE. ROUTE PLOT remains always INLINE and determines mandatory mode-specific geographic variables. All OPTIONAL user-selectable filters default to BYPASS. The initial plot is an overview; the USER can activate filters incrementally and re-plot.
2.2 Four selectable transport controls

Replace the transport dropdown with always-visible CHECKBOXES (not radio buttons). BY-SEA is USER-selected by default; BY-LAND, BY-RIB and BY-AIR begin unchecked. All modes are eligible for DISCOVERY: NERDS examines the waypoints and may activate necessary additional modes automatically. Distinguish USER-selected from automatically discovered status. There is no fifth MULTI-MODAL checkbox.
2.3 Mode-specific geographic routing & transfer points
BY-SEA: ocean passages, connected rivers/lakes/canals and larger watercraft; classify the actual vessel independently.
BY-RIB: smaller, shallower-draft watercraft; check craft-specific applicability, not a blanket shallow-water clearance guarantee.
BY-LAND: roads/tracks and real overland connections, not simple straight-line distance masquerading as roads.

1. Mission Statement

To provide safe, accurate & efficient marine navigation, primarily under sail and with the smallest possible ecological footprint, for our production & postproduction cast, crew, accommodations, facilities & equipment, to hundreds of destinations across our Earth — from readily accessible ports to the most remote locations reachable by vessel — throughout a potentially nine-year circumnavigation of our planet.
2. Purpose, Systems & Pre-Expedition Development

The successful execution of this mission requires the planning, coordination & management of an extraordinary combination of geographic, maritime, environmental, logistical, cultural, historical, scientific & production-related information.

To accomplish this, we are developing two complementary, homegrown systems: NERDS (Navigation & Expedition Research Discovery Surveyor), our principal USER INTERFACE, geographic discovery, editorial research & expedition mission-control application; and 4nR-SURVEYOR, our locally operated artificial intelligence gatekeeper & orchestrator, coordinating six specialised AI agents and their associated research and analytical capabilities.

Long before the expedition gets underway, NERDS & 4nR-SURVEYOR will play a central role in determining where The Faire Wind will travel, which destinations we will visit & why those destinations have been selected. Story Editors, Producers & Researchers will use NERDS’ detailed geographic and research filters, supported by SURVEYOR multidisciplinary investigations, to identify stories, subjects, communities, cultural connections & destinations throughout our Earth.

These discoveries will form the foundation upon which the production team determines the destinations, stories & communities of the expedition. NERDS & SURVEYOR will bring editorial and research priorities together with navigable geographic access, seasonal conditions, weather patterns, currents, passage times, logistics & the smallest possible ecological footprint. The initial itinerary — principal destinations, intermediate stops, passage sequence & production objectives — will be substantially established before The Faire Wind weighs anchor.

4nR-SURVEYOR will investigate how these destinations can be incorporated into the itinerary, while NERDS will present proposed routes for independent geographic verification, comparison & the Captain’s approval. Once underway, passage optimisation will continue in response to weather, tidal and ocean currents, time-of-day considerations, sea state, performance & energy factors. Route optimisation need not change the destination sequence; material changes to the approved itinerary remain subject to the Captain’s authority.

New discoveries during the voyage — conversations with people we meet, recommendations, YouTube audience contributions, scientific observations & unexpected encounters — may prompt research and proposed adjustments. The initial itinerary will be carefully planned. The expedition itself will remain open to discovery.
3. NERDS — Expedition Mission Control & Editorial Discovery

NERDS uses an interactive, zoomable globe and offline worldwide place search with disambiguation, optional online fallback, waypoint creation by search, map pin or coordinates, and geographic research filters across music, cuisine, history, culture, language, architecture, biology & environment. NERDS independently calculates and verifies geographic connectivity, route geometry & numerical results; displays up to ten comparative passage alternatives; manages waypoints, projects, vessel preferences, routing preferences, schedules and routes BY-SEA, BY-RIB, BY-LAND & BY-AIR. FULL TECHNICAL SCOPE & PRESERVED REQUIREMENTS
EXECUTIVE SCOPE — WHY THIS SYSTEM EXISTS

Faire Wind & Song (FWaS) is a nine-season worldwide maritime expedition in which music, cuisine, history, language, origins, culture and the natural environment inform where the expedition goes, whom it meets and what it documents. The central mission is: “Discovering & exploring our commonalities. Acknowledging & celebrating our uniqueness.” The companion principle is: “We are all the leaves of one tree.”

Its geographical mandate is expansive: investigate every destination The Faire Wind can potentially reach, including uninhabited islands, Antarctic research stations, reefs, small communities, remote rivers and historic sites. A location must not disappear from discovery because a population-filtered gazetteer does not contain it.

The expedition therefore requires two complementary locally operated software systems. NERDS is the planning and mission-control application used by the Captain and expedition team; 4nR-SURVEYOR is the independent AI intelligence service that researches, reasons, coordinates specialist agents, proposes alternatives and improves its methods through evidence and experience. Both applications have separate codebases and separately testable responsibilities.
MISSION OBJECTIVES & DELIVERABLES

1. Worldwide discovery — identify expedition-relevant places and their alternate names, coordinates, geographic relationships, provenance and practical research significance, regardless of population or remoteness.

2. Mission-driven research — investigate destinations and their music, cuisine, people, histories, origins, languages, architecture, biology and ecology; connect findings across disciplines rather than deliver disconnected answers.

3. Active voyage intelligence — support NERDS through CHEKOV with researched passage candidates, seasonal versus near-term environmental analysis, optional route comparisons and continuing reassessment when conditions change.

4. Independent verification — NERDS remains the authoritative route-calculation, geographic validation, distance/time accounting and Captain-facing plotting system. SURVEYOR proposals are inputs to be checked, not executable navigation authority.

5. Onboard local AI — run reasoning and specialist workflows primarily on AMD local compute through configurable inference runtimes, while retaining the two independent Starlink Maritime connections for retrieval, updates and wider services. Local AI is a chosen capability, not a claim that the ship lacks connectivity.

6. Multidisciplinary specialisation — operate six configurable suites: CHEKOV, EMERSON, BOURDAIN, CHAKOTAY, GOODALL and HADID, sharing well-governed evidence and requesting other specialists when a subject crosses disciplines.

7. Continuous improvement — identify failures and inferior performance, investigate root causes, change models/tools/workflows where warranted, retest against established methods and independent evidence, adopt demonstrated improvements and preserve rollback.

8. Expedition science & stewardship — collect instrumented environmental and vessel-performance observations with timestamps, locations, units, provenance, calibration and quality metadata, enabling long-term analysis and appropriately governed public sharing.

9. Reproducible engineering — deliver documented APIs, local model profiles, source-aware research records, automated benchmarks, deployment instructions and acceptance tests; distinguish implemented capabilities from development intentions.
SYSTEM RESPONSIBILITIES & OPERATING RELATIONSHIP

NERDS — Mission control: Captain-facing waypoint discovery and expedition projects; zoomable Cesium globe; sourced vector geographic data; connected routing; independently verified route geometry, distances, durations, ETAs and multimodal plans; persistent operation using its existing databases if SURVEYOR is unavailable.

4nR-SURVEYOR — Intelligence gatekeeper: accepts mission/research requests, interprets the task, delegates to appropriate suites, selects and operates locally available models and tools, manages evidence, returns structured findings and route proposals, performs quality assessment and coordinates learning. END-TO-END EXAMPLE: CAPTAIN REQUESTS A DESTINATION

The Captain enters “Lay in a course for Saint Peter & Saint Paul Rocks” in NERDS. NERDS resolves the current mission context and asks SURVEYOR to investigate. SURVEYOR delegates navigational research to CHEKOV and, where relevant, engages GOODALL, CHAKOTAY or another specialist. CHEKOV returns sourced candidate corridors and comparative assessments; NERDS checks the geographic connectivity and independently calculates routes, distances, voyage time and unresolved sections. The Captain reviews credible choices and approves one. As conditions change, SURVEYOR can propose a revision, but NERDS does not silently replace the approved course.

For a voyage six months away, analysis relies on climatology, seasonal patterns and qualified outlooks. For a passage tomorrow, it uses time-valid forecasts and observations. Vessel suitability restrictions are a separate ON/BYPASS advisory system during BETA, default BYPASS; the setting never permits routes across land or fabricated connected waterways.

System at a glance

4nR-SURVEYOR is a separate, locally operated AI research, orchestration and learning application for Faire Wind & Song. It dispatches work to six specialist suites: CHEKOV (navigation), EMERSON (music), BOURDAIN (cuisine), CHAKOTAY (human heritage), GOODALL (biology and environment), and HADID (architecture and engineering). I. PURPOSE, RESEARCH FOUNDATIONS & BASELINE REQUIREMENTS
1. Purpose & identity

4nR-SURVEYOR is the locally operated AI research intelligence within NERDS (Navigation & Expedition Research Discovery Surveyor), supporting the Faire Wind & Song global expedition. NERDS is the host application; 4nR-SURVEYOR is the agent; Qwen3 is the current foundation model; Lemonade is the current inference server. The agent name is configurable, independent of the underlying model.
Mission statement: “Discovering & exploring our commonalities. Acknowledging & celebrating our uniqueness.”
Companion principle: “We are all the leaves of one tree.”

The agent investigates relationships among peoples, places, music, cuisine, history, languages, cultural practices, environments & the routes that connect them. Its role is research, discovery, synthesis & source-aware interpretation. NERDS remains the system of record for approved user preferences, projects, waypoints and research findings.

3. Architectural principles
Offline-first: local research and inference remain useful at sea without continuous connectivity.
Store & Forward: acquire selected material when connected; index and reuse it offline. AI-CACHE (planned 8 TB NVMe) and AI-ARCHIVE (planned 80 TB usable RAID 6) are separate storage tiers.
User-approved scope: natural-language research directives are interpreted into detailed proposals, never silently promoted to approved master preferences.
A stable scholarly classification foundation underpins familiar user-facing labels and examples in parentheses.

Data-driven SURVEYOR modules: classification trees, option descriptions, aliases, source references and approval states belong in structured configuration/data rather than separate hard-coded dialogs.
Research outputs retain source provenance, geographical and temporal context; distinguish sourced evidence from inference.
Research computation and downloads are bounded by master preferences; discovery of a topic does not itself authorise a deep investigation.
4nR-SURVEYOR orchestrates research and supports navigation analysis; deterministic routing computations are separately testable software components.

II. MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE & OPERATIONS
1. Governing purpose & authority

4nR-SURVEYOR is an independently operable, locally hosted AI intelligence and orchestration platform serving Faire Wind & Song, NERDS and authorised research clients. NERDS is the expedition mission-control application, captain-facing interface and authoritative voyage state; 4nR-SURVEYOR is the AI gatekeeper directing six specialised suites. Neither application is merged into the other. NERDS retains full core route-planning and project operations when SURVEYOR is unavailable.

Architectural correction to v1.0: the v1.0 description of SURVEYOR as intelligence “within NERDS” means integrated service relationship, NOT an embedded dependency or common codebase. The applications are independent products joined by a versioned interface.

Human control: “We are driving the car, not getting run over by it.” The Captain and expedition team determine objectives and approve consequential decisions; recommendations do not silently override approved voyage plans.

6. CHEKOV — intelligent navigation & Captain’s route selection

NERDS receives the Captain’s destination and voyage priorities, issues a structured planning request to SURVEYOR, and SURVEYOR dispatches CHEKOV with supporting tools and agents. CHEKOV proposes up to TEN genuinely distinct candidate passages (fewer when evidence supports fewer). NERDS independently validates vector connectivity, calculates the actual route geometry, distance, duration, energy estimates where supported and identifies unknowns. The Captain compares candidates and approves the authoritative route.

Balanced Passage is multi-objective, weighing time, distance, weather, sea state, prevailing winds, currents, energy, navigational complexity and expedition priorities. Hard geographic connectivity is always enforced. Vessel suitability is a separate ON/BYPASS user preference, with BETA default BYPASS; enabling ON initially supplies advisories without rejecting valid geographic geometry. No arbitrary offshore access substitutions, invented links or route lines crossing land.
The Captain can request up to ten alternatives; each displays provenance, geometric verification result, NM, timing/uncertainty, weather basis, energy assumptions and reason for ranking.

Six-month planning uses seasonal climatology, historical distributions and probabilistic outlooks; near-term routing uses time-valid marine forecasts and observations; underway analysis uses updated data and telemetry.
NERDS verifies CHEKOV outputs with its independently testable vector graph and numerical methods. A rejected proposal returns structured diagnostics for further research and revision.

CHEKOV may evaluate AI-generated routes against established routing tools. Underperformance requires WHY analysis—data, assumptions, forecast, algorithms or workflows—then proposed improvements, repeatable retesting and measured promotion.
The selected route remains under Captain control. Active monitoring can propose changes promptly; it cannot silently replace the authorised route or directly command steering/propulsion.
NERDS retains vector-first routing and a geographically accurate zoomable Cesium globe showing waypoints and route polylines; accuracy outranks decorative imagery.
7. Learning & method improvement

Operational learning is explicit engineering work, not merely accumulating chat histories. Every suite shall preserve task inputs, sources, chosen models/tools, outputs, verification, measured outcomes, failure details and reasons for revisions. The learning cycle is EXECUTE → MEASURE → INVESTIGATE WHY → EXPERIMENT → RETEST → ADOPT OR REJECT → MONITOR.

SURVEYOR shall have the ability to investigate why an AI technique fails to exceed an established benchmark, formulate a new workflow or computational approach, test it against held-out and regression cases and retain proven improvements with rollback. Learning may change retrieval, prompts, algorithms, model choice, calibration or ultimately model weights where data justify training. Unverified self-modification is not promoted to production.
8. Observational science & open knowledge ambitions

The Faire Wind expedition should collect relevant weather, water and vessel operational observations wherever instrumentation allows: timestamped WGS84 position, course/speed, winds, pressure, temperature, humidity, waves, currents, water temperature/salinity as available, energy systems, propulsion and deviations from forecasts. GOODALL manages biological/environmental scientific analysis; CHEKOV uses navigation-relevant observations; SURVEYOR maintains long-term evidence and quality management.

Retain original measurements, calibration metadata, equipment details, timestamps, location, quality flags and derived estimates separately. Investigate openly sharing eligible observation datasets and potentially distributing a free maritime intelligence/navigation product in the future. Public release is subject to data licences, consent, privacy, provenance and research quality.

C. Runtime classes, compatibility & licence gates

CLASS 1 — Lemonade-first GGUF/llama.cpp inference. Start with the existing Qwen3-30B-A3B model and compatible supported checkpoints. Confirm exact model identifier and quantisation on the installed Lemonade release; the public model catalogue changes over time.

CLASS 2 — Multimodal vision and transcription. Evaluate Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Whisper large-v3-turbo where the chosen local backend supports the exact model and its preprocessing; otherwise isolate these services behind SURVEYOR adapters rather than assume Lemonade support.  [Source: Whisper]

CLASS 3 — Specialist scientific/audio models. Aurora and Music Flamingo are research/evaluation candidates with their own runtimes, input pipelines and usage constraints; do not assume they execute through Lemonade or are appropriate for unrestricted commercial deployment. For Music Flamingo, the checked release identifies non-commercial research use, and Aurora documentation notes non-academic usage concerns: confirm terms and obtain permissions as needed before deployment.  [Source: Music Flamingo]

CLASS 4 — Retrieval. Pilot Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B for compact multilingual indexing, compare 4B on difficult retrieval, and add a reranker if measurable. Do not replace source citations with embedding similarity scores.

CLASS 5 — Deterministic engines. Geodesy, connected vector topology, routing graph validation, energy accounting, CAD geometry and sensor calibration remain numerical computations used by agents. SURVEYOR may generate proposals and investigate failures; NERDS independently verifies course geometry and passage accounting.
D. Selection, experimentation & continuous learning contract

Each suite registers capabilities and one or more model profiles: model ID, version/checkpoint hash, licence, local runtime URL/adapter, context and quantisation, resource ceilings, tool permissions, specialist data indexes, benchmark profile, fallback profile and configuration revision.

On every task SURVEYOR selects an eligible model and records why. A task may invoke several specialists sequentially: for example, EMERSON transcribes an interview, analyses a recording and sends its sourced cultural context to CHAKOTAY.

Run benchmark datasets before adopting a model or model update. Maintain domain-specific holdout tests and production-like tasks. Compare with existing best methods, investigate where an AI workflow falls short, revise tools/prompts/models and retest. Record failure investigations as first-class evidence.

Promotion to operational use requires benchmark evidence, licence approval, offline/restart success, reproducibility, recoverable fallbacks and rollback. The six suites are not automatically authorised to update their own production model weights or routing algorithms.

Capacity planning must measure actual installed AMD system memory, concurrent model footprint and throughput. Schedule inference according to operational priority: CHEKOV time-sensitive route investigation ahead of background research, without silently discarding queued work.

I. Cross-suite model evaluation and active selection

An individual suite may register multiple models with distinct tasks; SURVEYOR chooses the candidate by capability, licence, verified local availability, context, data modality, latency, power and historical benchmark record. Selection reason and checkpoint hash shall accompany every task.

PER-CANDIDATE REGISTER: canonical model/checkpoint identifier, download/source URL, published date, version/hash, model owner, licence, intended use, selected inference runtime, model/quantisation format, input modalities, CPU/GPU/NPU memory and measured throughput, benchmark dataset, status owner, benchmark outcome, rejection reason and next evaluation action.

NO PERFORMANCE CLAIMS WITHOUT TESTS: statuses designate evaluation priority, not measured accuracy or a proven fit for installed AMD hardware. Every suite must maintain a best-known operational configuration and at least one fallback or deterministic alternative.

LICENCE GATES: differentiate source-code licences from model checkpoint/data licences. Music Flamingo is non-commercial research in the reviewed release; Aurora documentation indicates an open research model but directs commercial use enquiries separately. Neither is silently promoted to unrestricted deployment.

Cross-suite reuse: SURVEYOR, CHEKOV and GOODALL may share one Aurora inference service when supported; EMERSON and CHAKOTAY may share one Whisper service. Duplicate model processes are avoided where safe; each suite maintains separate datasets and evaluation tasks.

Performance and power: record actual idle/loaded memory, model swapping, response latency, energy, context-window behaviour and task completion on the AMD hardware in hand. Do not presume NPU deployment when a checkpoint requires PyTorch/GPU execution.

Improvement cycle: benchmark → diagnose underperformance → research alternative checkpoints/workflows/data → experiment → retest on holdout cases → promote with audit record and rollback. Preserve failures as training and evaluation evidence, not as silent model substitutions.

6A. Offshore routing & dual voyage estimates — approved requirements

Default speeds — The expedition-wide reference speed is 6.0 knots, editable in VESSEL PREFERENCES. The nominal target cruising speed under POWER-DIESEL or POWER-ELECTRIC is 10.0 knots, also editable. These are planning assumptions, not guaranteed actual speeds.

Side-by-side passage display — For every leg and the whole voyage, display STANDARD (6.0 kn) and CALCULATED estimates adjacent to one another. Show reference speed, modelled effective speed over ground (SOG), passage distance (NM), elapsed duration, projected arrival date/time and the time difference. Never replace the 6-knot baseline with the calculated figure.

Power-mode accounting — When powered propulsion is selected, use the 10.0-knot nominal target as an input to the calculated passage case; retain the 6.0-knot baseline for direct comparison. Sailing nominal target begins at 6.0 kn. For mixed sail/power routing, compute elapsed time by segment according to its operating mode and integrate segment times rather than averaging segment speeds.

Dynamic recalculation — Recalculate the CALCULATED estimate after changes to route geometry, distance, propulsion mode, vessel preferences or available wind/current/wave data. Until numerical environmental integration is available, calculate a clearly labelled nominal-speed estimate; do not display synthetic weather-derived values as measured or forecast speeds.

Penalise unnecessary coastline proximity, mapped reefs/shoals and unsuitable or uncertain depths; consider continental shelf, shelf break, slope and abrupt seabed rises as contextual factors. Coastal separation — Provide an editable preferred minimum separation from land in nautical miles (suggested choices: 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 and Custom). This is a soft optimisation preference, not an absolute constraint, particularly for harbour approaches, canals, straits and rivers.

Detect charted underwater obstructions where data supports them. Geological/seismic/volcanic hazards, if added later, require their own datasets; seabed gradients alone do not predict activity.
